summary: Brass: Birmingham is a dense economic Euro where you build canal and rail networks while flipping industry tiles for points across two historical eras. It's a tight, punishing engine of loans, markets, and network-building that rewards careful sequencing.
praised: Extremely high replayability and strategic depth
Gorgeous, thematic production and map design
criticised: Steep learning curve, unforgiving for new players
Can feel like multiplayer solitaire with only indirect interaction

interaction.detail: Players compete indirectly for space on a shared map and for limited resources in a shared coal/iron market, so building near or ahead of opponents can starve their options. Most of the tension comes from anticipating others' moves rather than direct conflict.

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Everything you do ultimately cashes out through just two tallies — the VP printed on your canal/rail links and the VP printed on your flipped industry tiles — scored once at the end of each era.
scoring.how_you_win: Build and flip (sell or use) industry tiles from six different industries while extending your canal and rail network across the canal and rail eras; the player with the highest combined link-and-industry VP after the rail era wins.
